body:
## Why

The post-merge verifier compares a PR against a diff that includes sibling PRs merged into the base branch between PR creation and merge. This misattributes files, can truncate the real subject files, and can cause incorrect closer-lane verdicts.

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js:614-621` uses `pull.base.sha` with `pull.merge_commit_sha`; `fetchLocalGitDiff` uses `git diff ${baseSha}...${headSha}`. Because the merge commit is on the base branch and `base.sha` is its ancestor, the range sweeps intervening base-branch history instead of only the PR diff. The fallback `fetchPullRequestDiff` is correct but runs only when the local diff is empty.

Observed in `stranske/learning-management-system` on 2026-09-10: #662 had no intervening merge and produced a correct report; #663 included #662's files; #665 included #663's files. Contamination also consumed `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS` (300000), truncating subject files. This affects every consumer of `stranske/Workflows/.github/workflows/reusable-agents-verifier.yml@main`.

## Scope

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js`, `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` (byte-identical and changed in lockstep), and `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js`.

## Non-Goals

Do not change the provider prompt, verdict schema, or `verifier_verdict_json.py`.

Do not raise diff character or byte budgets.

Do not retro-verify already-closed issues; LMS #656, #658, and the #663/#665 PR threads remain dispositioned.

A documentation-only comment without changing the range does not satisfy this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the diff range in `.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js:614-621` so merged-PR context contains only that PR's diff.
- [ ] Update `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` with the identical change and keep it byte-identical to `.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js`.
- [ ] Add a test in `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` stubbing `execFile`/`pulls.get` for a merged PR with one sibling commit after `base.sha`, asserting the diff includes the PR file and excludes the sibling file.
- [ ] Add a test in `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` asserting `### File changes` lists exactly the PR's files.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a merged PR with sibling commits between `base.sha` and `merge_commit_sha`, generated `## PR Diff (full)` and `### File changes` contain only the PR's files.
- [ ] Existing unmerged/push-path cases in `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` pass unchanged.
- [ ] `npm test` or the repository JS test entry point passes for `.github/scripts/__tests__/`.
- [ ] Restoring `baseSha = pull.base?.sha` as the range left side makes the sibling-contamination test fail naming the sibling file; reverting makes it pass, with both transcripts recorded.
- [ ] A merged PR with an advanced base branch produces a provider-comparison report without an “unrelated changes” or “scope creep” caveat naming a file the PR does not touch.

## Implementation Notes

For merged PRs, use the merge commit’s first parent as the diff base: `${headSha}^` for squash merges or `git diff ${headSha}^1 ${headSha}` for merge commits. Do not use `pull.base.sha` as the left side when the right side is a base-branch merge commit.

Alternatively, prefer `fetchPullRequestDiff` for merged PRs and retain `fetchLocalGitDiff` only for unmerged/push paths. The REST diff is authoritative and the function already exists.

Explicitly guard the degenerate case where `merge-base(baseSha, headSha) === baseSha` and `headSha` is reachable from the base branch; document why the three-dot range is not the PR diff.

Do not raise `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS`; truncation is a symptom of contamination.

````text
<!-- workflow-source:local_request -->

## Why

The post-merge verifier grades a PR against a diff that also contains **every sibling PR merged into the base branch between that PR's creation and its own merge**. The verdict-bearing provider-comparison report therefore attributes other PRs' files to the PR under review, and — because the contaminated diff is larger — truncates the real subject files out of the context window. The closer lane closes source issues on these verdicts.

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js:614-621`:

```js
const baseSha = pull.base?.sha;
const headSha = pull.merge_commit_sha || pull.head?.sha || targetSha;
let diffText = fetchLocalGitDiff({ baseSha, headSha, ... });
```

`fetchLocalGitDiff` (line 218) runs `git diff --no-color ${baseSha}...${headSha}`. The three-dot form means `merge-base(baseSha, headSha)..headSha`. But `headSha` is `pull.merge_commit_sha`, a commit **on the base branch**, and `pull.base.sha` is an ancestor of it — GitHub records `base.sha` as the base-ref tip when the PR is opened and does not advance it as the branch moves. So `merge-base(base.sha, merge_commit) == base.sha`, the three-dot form degenerates to two-dot, and the range sweeps the whole stretch of base-branch history in between. The fallback immediately below (`fetchPullRequestDiff`, line 237, `pulls.get` with `mediaType: {format: 'diff'}`) returns the correct PR-only diff, but it runs only when the local diff comes back empty — and with `fetch-depth: 0` in `reusable-agents-verifier.yml:105` the local path succeeds, so the correct implementation is never reached.

## Observed instances (2026-09-10, stranske/learning-management-system)

Three consecutive verifier runs, with a natural control:

| PR | `base.sha` | `merge_commit_sha` | merged in between | report claimed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #662 | `89bad27009bc` | `0ebc108e1622` | *nothing* | correct — **no contamination caveat** |
| #663 | `89bad27009bc` | `ba28a8d418fd` | #662 (`0ebc108`) | *"also modifies `src/lms/maintenance/drafts.py` and adds `test_draft_approval.py`, `test_maintenance_loop_e2e.py` … this is scope creep"* — those are #662's files |
| #665 | `0ebc108e1622` | `c96e79170609` | #663 (`ba28a8d4`) | *"bundles unrelated changes to `src/lms/scheduling/repository.py` and associated scheduling test files (+90/-11, +73/-1)"* — those are #663's two test files, matching its line counts exactly |

#663's actual diff is three files (`src/lms/scheduling/repository.py` +19/-1 and two `tests/scheduling/` files); #665's is four files, none under `src/lms/scheduling/`. #662, with nothing merged in between, produced a clean report — which is what makes the mechanism, not coincidence, the explanation.

The harm compounds. Both reports also carried a caveat that the *real* subject file was truncated out of the context ("The full diff for `src/lms/scheduling/repository.py` … was truncated in the provided context, so the exact validation logic … could not be directly inspected"). That is the same cause: `formatDiffForContext` truncates at `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS` (300000, line 19), and the sibling commits consume the budget. So the verifier grades on files that are not the PR's while losing the files that are.

Both verdicts happened to be PASS, so nothing was mis-closed this time. The failure mode is not benign: an arm that sees a sibling's unrelated diff can lower confidence (both anthropic verdicts dropped to 68% and 72% on the contamination caveat), report scope creep that does not exist, or FAIL a PR for not implementing criteria while looking at another PR's files. The exposure is fleet-wide — every consumer repo calls `stranske/Workflows/.github/workflows/reusable-agents-verifier.yml@main`, and the rapid-merge cadence the lanes run at is exactly the condition that triggers it.

## Scope

`.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` and its mirror `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` (currently byte-identical; both must change in lockstep), plus `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js`.

## Implementation Notes

1. The correct base for a merged PR's own diff is the merge commit's **first parent**: `${headSha}^` when `headSha` is `pull.merge_commit_sha`. For a squash merge that is exactly the PR's contribution; for a merge commit, `git diff ${headSha}^1 ${headSha}` is likewise the PR's contribution. Do not keep using `pull.base.sha` as the left side of a range whose right side is on the base branch.
2. Alternatively — and more simply — prefer `fetchPullRequestDiff` for the merged-PR case and keep `fetchLocalGitDiff` only for the unmerged/push path where no PR diff endpoint applies. The REST diff is authoritative for "what this PR changed" and the function already exists.
3. Whichever is chosen, guard the degenerate case explicitly: if `merge-base(baseSha, headSha) === baseSha` **and** `headSha` is reachable from the base branch, the three-dot range is not the PR's diff. A comment saying so is worth more than the fix, because the three-dot form looks correct on inspection.
4. Do not raise `DEFAULT_DIFF_MAX_CHARS` as the remedy. A larger budget hides the contamination instead of removing it, and the truncation caveat is a symptom.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the diff range in `agents_verifier_context.js:614-621` so a merged PR's context contains only that PR's diff.
- [ ] Mirror the identical change into `templates/consumer-repo/.github/scripts/agents_verifier_context.js` and confirm the two files stay byte-identical.
- [ ] Add a case to `.github/scripts/__tests__/agents-verifier-context.test.js` that stubs `execFile`/`pulls.get` for a merged PR whose base branch advanced by one sibling commit after `base.sha`, and asserts the produced diff contains the PR's own file and **not** the sibling's.
- [ ] Add a case asserting the emitted `### File changes` summary lists exactly the PR's files, since that summary is what the provider prompt leans on when the full diff is truncated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For a merged PR with sibling commits between `base.sha` and `merge_commit_sha`, the generated context's `## PR Diff (full)` block and `### File changes` summary both list only the PR's own files.
- [ ] The unmerged/push path is unchanged: no regression in the existing `agents-verifier-context.test.js` cases.
- [ ] `npm test` (or the repo's JS test entry point) passes for `.github/scripts/__tests__/`.
- [ ] Deliberate-break: restore `baseSha = pull.base?.sha` as the range's left side and confirm the new sibling-contamination test fails naming the sibling's file; revert and confirm green. Quote both transcripts.
- [ ] Re-verification evidence: after the fix, one merged PR in a repo with an advanced base branch produces a provider-comparison report with no "unrelated changes"/"scope creep" caveat naming a file the PR does not touch.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the provider prompt, the verdict schema, or `verifier_verdict_json.py`.
- Do not raise the diff character or byte budgets.
- Do not retro-verify already-closed issues; the three instances above are dispositioned in place (LMS #656, #658 and the #663/#665 PR threads).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a comment documenting the three-dot degeneration without changing the range leaves every future report contaminated.
````
